lawyer: Syed Mamun Mahbub, Advocate with Zainul Abedin, Advocate For the Petitioners. Mahbubey Alam, Attorney-General, with Murad Reza, Add Attorney-General Israt Jahan, AAG Kashefa Hussain, AAG—For the Respondents.
parties:
Nuran Nabi and others ------ Petitioners
Vs
Government of Bangladesh and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment: 11. Inter-ministerial exchanges between the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Finance from 12-1-2011 to 11-9-2011 reveal further in particular, the Ministry of Finance's displeasure with the manner in which the Government, from that Ministry's point of view, now risks being saddled unduly with a financial burden that could have easily been avoided should the Ministry of Education have exercised greater prudence for its part in respect to principally two matters. First, there is raised the issue of a perceived lack of prudence evident ostensibly in the Ministry of Education having acted far too generously by granting time scale to all non-government college and Madrasa teachers in November-December, 2010 over and beyond the sixty-two petitioners in Writ Petition No. 5390 of 2007. Questioned also is the absence of any initiative on the part of the Ministry of Education to appeal against the High Court's judgment in Writ Petition No. 5390 of 2007. Second, evident also is the dissatisfaction of the Ministry of Finance with MPO provisions being written into the ২০১০ র্নিদেশিকা WPM apparently at the sole initiative of the Ministry of Education without prior consultation with the Ministry of Finance. Given the reality on the ground, however, of the ২০১০ র্নিদেশিকা being presently in effect, the Ministry of Finance appears willing to concede the acceptance, only in principle, of the existence and currency of the ২০১০ র্নিদেশিকা while being firmly adamant in not releasing any fund to meet the financial obligations imposed there under. It is evident that the Ministry of Finance has, therefore, left it entirely to the Ministry of Education to scout for necessary and additional funds if, as and when the Ministry of Education selects to meet the demands of numerous individuals finding themselves in the same predicament as the nine Petitioners. As asserted by Dr Chowdhury in Court on 19-2-2012, and as comes across clearly in his Affidavit-in-Opposition, the best that the Ministry of Education has been able to muster, as per the proposal of the Ministry of Finance, has been the creation of a fund by আন্তঃখাত সমন্বয় or internal adjustment within the resource ceiling set for the Ministry of Education. That fund, however, declaredly will only go so far as meeting the salaries and benefits of individuals like the nine petitioners at their respective entitled scale at Grade 6 prospectively from February 2012 onwards. It is specifically declared in the Affidavit-in-opposition that the petitioners will be entitled to get their salaries and other benefits at the scale of pay Grade 6 as per clause 11(kha) of the ২০১০ র্নিদেশিকা with the important qualification that such payments will be made prospectively as of February, 2012 simply by reason of the storage and/or limitation of funds available for that purpose, thereby, wholly negating any claim or entitlement to payment of such salary or benefit in arrears. Interestingly, the Secretary, Ministry of Education, submits that under this scenario the principle of natural justice will not have been violated vis-a-vis the petitioners.
